summary:
Abandoned Legacy is an interactive educational web platform developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, addressing the challenge “Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars.”

The platform transforms the history of inactive lunar and Martian exploration equipment into an engaging multimedia experience. It features first-person storytelling based on historical mission records, a real-time chronometer tracking the time since selected missions' final communications, an interactive mission explorer, technical instrument dossiers, a historical timeline, and a scientific discoveries matrix. Browser-based audio synthesis and speech narration bring these silent explorers to life.
By presenting their engineering achievements and scientific contributions in an accessible format, Abandoned Legacy challenges the perception of these machines as forgotten space debris. It highlights how their discoveries continue to contribute to our understanding of the Moon and Mars, making planetary exploration history more engaging and accessible to students, educators, and the public.
details:
Project Details — Abandoned Legacy

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

Abandoned Legacy is an interactive educational web platform that preserves the scientific and historical legacy of inactive lunar and Martian exploration equipment. It transforms historical NASA mission records, engineering achievements, and scientific discoveries into an accessible multimedia storytelling experience.

The platform consists of several interactive sections:

  • Mission Explorer: Allows visitors to search and filter seven mission profiles by destination, including the Moon, Mars, and Deep Space. Each profile provides operational lifespan comparisons, landing locations, and technical information.
  • Chronometer of Silence: Displays live elapsed-time counters showing how long it has been since the final recorded communications of five selected missions: Apollo ALSEP, Viking 1, Mars Pathfinder and Sojourner, Spirit, and Opportunity.
  • Voices from the Silence: Presents first-person narratives based on historical mission records, allowing visitors to explore each spacecraft's journey, discoveries, and final moments. Users can listen through browser-based speech synthesis or explore reconstructed telemetry-style displays.
  • Mission Timeline: Presents important milestones in planetary exploration chronologically, connecting historical missions with the broader history of space exploration.
  • Scientific Discoveries Matrix: Highlights important findings from these missions and explains their continuing relevance to planetary science.
  • Technical Dossiers: Provides detailed information about scientific instruments, their functions, technical specifications, and mission records.

The website also features synthesized radio carrier tones generated directly in the browser, creating an immersive experience inspired by deep-space communication.

2. What benefits does it provide?

Abandoned Legacy makes complex planetary exploration history easier to understand and explore. Instead of presenting spacecraft merely as inactive hardware, it highlights their engineering achievements and scientific contributions.

Students and educators can learn about real scientific instruments such as Alpha Particle X-Ray Spectrometers (APXS), Mössbauer Spectrometers, and seismic experiments. Comparisons between planned and actual mission lifespans also demonstrate engineering endurance and the challenges of operating robotic equipment in extreme environments.

The platform combines scientific information with storytelling, making historical mission archives more engaging and accessible to the general public.

3. What is the intended impact?

The project's primary goal is to change how people perceive decommissioned planetary exploration equipment. These machines may have stopped transmitting, but their discoveries continue to contribute to our understanding of other worlds.

By connecting historical missions with modern exploration, Abandoned Legacy encourages curiosity about planetary science, space engineering, and scientific research. It also aims to serve as an educational resource for students, teachers, and space enthusiasts.

4. What tools and technologies were used?

The project was developed as a responsive, client-side Single Page Application using:

  • React 19: Building the interactive user interface.
  • TypeScript: Structuring the application with static typing.
  • Vite: Development and build environment.
  • Tailwind CSS v4: Responsive styling and visual design.
  • Lucide React: Interface icons.
  • Web Audio API: Generating radio carrier tones and audio effects directly in the browser.
  • Web Speech API: Providing browser-native text-to-speech narration.
  • Google AI Studio: Assisting with code development, debugging, and AI-generated visual illustrations.
  • Google Cloud Run: Hosting the deployed application.

The application uses static mission data and does not require a backend, database, external API connection, or runtime AI model to function.

5. How is the project creative and innovative?

The central creative idea is to give silent exploration machines a voice. The first-person storytelling approach transforms technical mission histories into narratives that visitors can connect with emotionally.

The Chronometer of Silence turns the passage of time since a spacecraft's final communication into an interactive experience. Synthesized radio carrier tones and telemetry-style displays further recreate the atmosphere of deep-space communication.

The combination of historical records, interactive technical information, scientific discoveries, and storytelling creates a different way to experience planetary exploration history.

6. What factors did the team consider?

During development, we considered scientific accuracy, accessibility, usability, technical feasibility, and transparency.

Historical information and scientific findings were cross-referenced with publicly available resources from NASA JPL, NASA NSSDCA, the Lunar and Planetary Institute, and the NASA Planetary Data System.

We also prioritized a responsive interface that works across desktop, tablet, and mobile devices without requiring installation, user accounts, or external API access.

AI-generated illustrations are used as visual representations rather than authentic NASA archival photographs. AI assistance was also used during development and in structuring the storytelling content, while the deployed application itself does not use runtime AI.

Overall, Abandoned Legacy aims to preserve the stories of planetary exploration pioneers and make their scientific legacy accessible to future generations.
